summary.value: The Ashen people have built their cities around the Living Pyre, a sentient communal hearth and lighthouse that has warmed them for millennia. Its imp-pyro wisps are sparks that carry heat out to homes and furnaces — and, in emergencies, stand as warden turrets along the shrine's approaches. Hearth culture runs deep: no Ashen home is without a flame lit from the Pyre's own.

sharedOpinions.reason: He struck at our hearth and called our warmth a siege engine. A city does not forgive a hand at its fire, but the law still governs ours.
The Court is our civic ground — our furnaces, statues, and workshops. When its bells ring, our wardens answer.
The Colossus's heating stones keep our outlying homes warm when the Pyre's light runs thin. Firefolk understand firefolk.

metaphorDomain.source: hearth, lamplight, embers, warmth carried home

examples.value: No one owns a flame; you only carry it a while.
A cold house is a question nobody answered.

meaning.value: A flame lit directly from the Living Pyre and carried home to seed a family's own hearth. The wisps' nightly errand.
The millennia the Pyre has burned for the cities; the Ashen measure their history in it the way others count kings.

customs.value: Guests are offered a coal from the hearth to carry to their own fire — the deepest courtesy an Ashen household can give.
On storm nights every household keeps a lamp in the window, answering the Pyre's beacon so no traveler walks unguided.

taboos.value: Never deliberately put out another's hearth-fire. It is the closest thing the Ashen have to a crime.
Never raise a weapon within sight of the Pyre. It has warmed ten thousand years of children; it will not be menaced.
